relevance_note: Case report of a Chinese family in which a PSTPIP1 missense variant was found: "a missense mutation in exon 11 of thePSTPIP1 gene (c.748G>C; p.E250Q) was detected in the boy, his younger brother and his father".
method_note: Read in full and built by hand in a small Python script (no table transcription by script). Labels III-1, III-2, II-1, I-1 are the pedigree labels from Figure 1 and Table 1 (Table 1 has the brothers as columns: column headers 'III-1' and 'III-2'). The mother is mentioned only as unaffected ('not his parents') and is not stated to be tested, so she gets no row. One previously published person described with individual-level features in the Discussion (Sardana et al[21]) is included as 'ref [21] patient'; the literature summary of 52 cases (Figures 2-3) gives no individual-level data. Contradictions/errors in the paper: (1) Outcome section says 'In November 2019, tocilizumab, the humanized anti-TNF-α monoclonal antibody' whereas the Treatment section says adalimumab followed tocilizumab; the Discussion says 'Our patients were treated with adamumab for 6 mo'. (2) Figure 1B legend gives 'p.748 G>C' and the WES paragraph says 'amino acid position 748' while the protein change is p.Glu250Gln/E250Q; the cDNA c.748G>C from the Abstract and Conclusion is recorded. (3) Figure 1A legend says 'autosomal dominant hyponatremia pedigree'. (4) Grandfather I-1: text is hedged ('might also have similar symptoms'), the figure legend is not ('had the similar symptoms'); recorded observed from the legend. Zygosity 'heterozygosity' is recorded only for the proband (sentence follows the proband's WES); it is not clearly stated for III-2 or II-1. Inheritance 'inherited paternal' for both brothers from the statement that their father carries the same missense variant. Functional evidence is literature-cited (refs [24] and [2]) for E250Q, not an assay in this study. Normal findings (D-27): 'Routine test results for complete blood count, liver and kidney function, and electrolytes were normal' is recorded as a whole (abnormal complete blood count/liver/kidney function/electrolytes excluded); anemia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia and kidney involvement are left not reported. Normal immune tests are recorded as each named test excluded. Fever excluded for III-1 rests on a single body temperature (36.2 °C) at physical examination. The knee abscess drained in III-1 is not counted as a skin or soft-tissue abscess (checklist not reported). Table 1 IL-8 and IL-10 values are not recorded as features (the text names only IL-1, IL-6 and TNF-α as elevated). For III-2 the cytokine elevation rests on 'Our cases show similar changes (Table 1)' plus his Table 1 column; the absence of skin features rests on 'our patients only suffer from pyogenic arthritis at present' (the paper's two patients, the brothers). For II-1 the checklist exclusions (arthritis, pyoderma gangrenosum, acne, hidradenitis suppurativa, skin abscesses, fever) rest on 'their father did not show clinical symptoms' and the legend 'without symptoms'; laboratory and organ items are left not reported. n_patients_reported is null because the authors give no number (two affected brothers plus an asymptomatic carrier father are described).

treatment_summary.value: glucocorticoids, antibiotics and surgeries; incision and drainage of the abscess with 20-d anti-infection treatment and joint cavity irrigation; tocilizumab 12 mg/kg IV every 4 wk for about 6 mo, then adalimumab 20 mg SC every 2 wk; intra-articular triamcinolone hexacetonide in the recent episode
span: Treatments, such as glucocorticoids, antibiotics, even surgeries could alleviate joints pain and swelling to some extent but could not inhibit the recurrence of arthritis.
The incision and drainage of the abscess was performed. With a 20-d treatment of anti-infection and joint cavity irrigation after the surgery, the symptoms were relieved.
The patient received tocilizumab (12 mg/kg intravenously) every 4 wk for about 6 mo. After that, adalimumab was given (20 mg subcutaneously) every 2 wk successively.
In the recent episode, the rapid relief was achieved by intra-articular triamcinolone hexacetonide.
Our patients were treated with adamumab for 6 mo, and their joint symptoms were alleviated quickly.

functional_evidence_statement.value: Literature-reported (refs [24], [2]), not tested in this study: E250Q disrupts binding of PTP-PEST to PSTPIP1, leading to PSTPIP1 hyperphosphorylation and higher affinity for pyrin (yeast two-hybrid and binding studies)
span: Yeast two-hybrid interaction trap assays revealed that two dominantly inherited missense mutations, A230T and E250Q, in the proline-serine-threonine phosphatase-interacting protein 1 [PSTPIP1, or CD2-binding protein 1 (CD2BP1)] gene were the pathogenesis[24].

The PAPA syndrome-associated A230T and E250Q mutations interfere with the binding of PEST-type protein tyrosine phosphatase (PTP-PSTP) to PSTPIP1, leading to the hyperphosphorylation of PSTPIP1, which have a higher affinity for pyrin than non-mutated forms[2].
